reference: Contract expectations use Bash's documented `type` and `help` builtin behavior plus the checked-in notify builtin documentation and its explicit --help output. The builtin documentation records the supported send syntax and socket forms. No result is copied from the candidate. `systemd-notify` is not a same-interface oracle for `notify send SOCKET PAYLOAD`, so runnable operation parity is unavailable.
coverage: Bash reports notify as a builtin through both type -t and type.
Bash help exposes the documented notify purpose, syntax, and division of responsibility.
The documented long and short help switches return their usage text.
exclusions: AF_UNIX datagram sends, filesystem and abstract address encoding, and syscall failure paths are DEFERRED under the task's operation-safety requirement; no notify send operation is run here.
There is no matching GNU CLI for this builtin's send subcommand. systemd-notify has a different interface and is not treated as direct parity.
The --version string is not independently specified in the reviewed docs, so it is not asserted.

cases.purpose: Check Bash's type -t contract for a compiled-in notify builtin.
Check Bash's user-facing type description for notify.
Check that help notify includes the documented purpose, syntax, and parser ownership without depending on Bash's help layout.
cases.script:
doc=$(help notify)
[[ $doc == *"Send sd_notify-style AF_UNIX datagrams."* ]]
[[ $doc == *"notify send SOCKET PAYLOAD"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"systemd-notify.sh owns CLI parsing;"* ]]

cases.purpose: Check the documented --help usage lines as stable public help output.
Check that the documented -h alias emits the same usage text as --help.
Verify a successful filesystem-path AF_UNIX datagram send and byte-exact payload delivery, including an embedded newline.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM or reviewed private socket fixture that owns a filesystem AF_UNIX SOCK_DGRAM receiver and independently checks exactly one byte-exact datagram. This task requires notify send operations to remain deferred.

cases.purpose: Verify systemd's @name spelling maps to the expected Linux abstract AF_UNIX address and delivers one exact datagram.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM or reviewed private abstract-namespace receiver fixture. The fixture must bind only its own abstract name and check exact datagram bytes; no system service or ambient socket may be contacted. This task requires notify send operations to remain deferred.

cases.purpose: Qualify empty and overlong socket names, an unavailable destination, and descriptor/error handling on send failure.
cases.reason: Requires a future reviewed syscall mock or disposable Linux VM with deterministic socket/sendto failures. It must verify invalid names fail before socket creation, failed sends return nonzero with a diagnostic, and descriptors are closed; no real endpoint may be used. This task requires notify send operations to remain deferred.
